n-creator-fee-routing.title: Creator fees routed to people
n-creator-fee-routing.summary: Coins whose metadata says their creator or trading fees are routed to a named person or account. UsePaid's page (usepaid.app, scraped 2026-10-13) says it routes each coin's creator fees to the X account the coin is launched for, held for that user to claim; MarsX and slopcannon say "Fees to @arikuschnir via UsePaid" and "Fees to @boneGPT via UsePaid". TeleMoney (TM) says it launches coins on pump.fun with fees redirected to any Telegram username, and @TeleMoneySOL posted on 2026-10-12 that 108 coins had launched, 262.8 SOL of creator fees had been generated and 17,411.2 GRAM paid out. Cashed Money (CASHED, pons on Robinhood Chain) says "Fees to @GetCashedMoney via Cashed", WIRED (Flap, BNB Chain) says token launches have fees wired to social media accounts, and Pepper The Raccoon says it redirects fees to its owner. A 2026-10-12 @PickACycle post says a pump.fun coin's fees can now be split between UsePaid, OTC desks and agencypad. The pools date from 2026-09-18 (Cashed Money) to 2026-10-12 (MarsX, about 12 hours before discovery). These are the projects' and traders' own claims: payouts are not verified, no affiliation among the coins was checked, and MarsX traded over 10x its market cap. Measured: six coins across all their pools.

summaries.n-tokenized-assets: Coins whose metadata describes tokenized stocks or real-world assets (RWAs). @RobinhoodCrypto posted on 2026-10-08 that it is exploring a Stock Token linked to an actively managed ETF with T. Rowe Price DA ("if successful"), and on 2026-09-08 that Robinhood Stock Tokens had reached $150M in TVL on Robinhood Chain. Apps built around those tokens have coins of their own: Borro.Markets (BORRO; "Lend, borrow and short stock tokens"), HyperDex (HYDX; "Unified Marketplace for Tokenized Assets & RWAs"), Prism Assets (PRISM; "tokenising real-world assets with AI"), Longbow (BOW; borrow USDG against tokenized stocks and RWAs), Quanta Pools (QUANTA; liquidity across Stock Tokens and RWAs), Mintfolio (MINTFOLIO; baskets of stocks and ETFs), opcode (OP; "The RWA prop AMM for every chain"), TARTAGLIA (TATA; "ZK dark pool for tokenized stocks"), and two pons coins created on 2026-10-11, HUME MARKETS (HUME; "Tokenized stocks, all in one place. Perps. Options. Lending & Borrowing.") and Ballast (BLLS; "Stock Token portfolios on @Robinhoodapp that rebalance themselves"). On Solana, Tokenize Everything (EVERYTHING; pool created 2026-10-07) describes tokenized RWAs as the biggest crypto meta of the last year and a half; one 2026-10-07 post by @RaOnChain called it a scam. None of the coins is shown to be issued by or affiliated with Robinhood, and their product descriptions are their own claims. VERDEX (VERDEX; "The front door to tokenized markets. 226 real-world assets, 12 issuers, 70 chains, one order.", pons) was added on 2026-10-13. Measured: twelve coins across all their pools.
summaries.n-super-intelligence: On Sept. 29 Trump said AI would officially be renamed "Super Intelligence" (Fox News). On 2026-10-04 the official @WhiteHouse account posted an announcement of a "Super Intelligence Force (SIF)", and Watcher.Guru and an @wallstreetbets post reported Elon Musk saying SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI. Super Inu ($SI), launched Sept. 21, re-pitched itself around the term; other coins followed, including another SI on pump.fun, 四 ("four", read as SI) on four.meme, Super Intelligence Force (SIF), Superintelligence Owl, two SpaceXSI coins on StonkFun, SpaceX Inu ($SI on Flap), Act II: The SI Prophecy, SuperHooks, two newer pump.fun coins, SpaceX Super Intelligence (SPACEXSI) and My Super Intelligent Cat (Ollie), whose metadata names the term, and two BNB Chain coins on Flap named TeslaSI ("Tesla Super Intelligence", pool created 2026-10-11, and a second whose Chinese metadata says it follows the SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI rename). None is shown to be affiliated with the announcements. Smaller coins named for SpaceXSI under the $100K market cap bar are not counted. Measured: sixteen coins across all their pools.
summaries.n-credits-for-holders: Coins that describe turning trading fees into AI model credits for holders. Orbio (orbio.so) says it sells LLM credits at a discount, that the discount comes from Orbio holders who offer unused credit, and that requests are relayed through its managed OpenRouter account; its coin ORBIO (pons, Robinhood Chain) says half of trading fees are converted into inference credits paid to holders. API (pump.fun) says fees are split by holdings and holders can claim SOL or 1.5x credits for GPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini through one OpenAI-compatible API; LLMPad (LLM, pump.fun) says it lets anyone launch model tokens or trading agents and generate LLM credits; bInference (BINF, Flap, BNB Chain) says an agent token's fees pay for the agent's AI and that credits bought with BNB are up to 8% cheaper with $BINF. Public posts from 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 compare BINF and API with ORBIO, and a rival project, DecentraMind, says ORBIO pioneered the model it builds on. The ORBIO and BINF pools date from 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-30; the API and LLM pools were created on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10. These are the projects' and traders' own claims: payouts, discounts and usage are not verified, no affiliation among the coins was checked, and one post says 11 bundles bought 62% of LLM's supply around its launch. Measured: four coins across all their pools.

On 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-12 @TeleMoneySOL said coins launched on its site pay creator fees to any Telegram @username in GRAM, reporting 108 coins launched, 262.8 SOL of creator fees generated and 17,411.2 GRAM paid out; @TeleMoneySOL's 2026-10-11 post says almost all coins that pay their creators pay X accounts. On 2026-10-12 @PickACycle said a pump.fun coin's fees can now be split between UsePaid, OTC desks and agencypad, and on 2026-10-07 @Joindotfun announced a waitlist for launching a coin for any creator and sending the fees to them (e3:1, e3:3).
n-creator-fee-routing.interpretation: Several launch tools pitch the same mechanism, creator fees paid to a named account or person, and new tools keep appearing, which is why this is treated as a shared story. The figures are the projects' own and payouts are not verified. The coins are not shown to be affiliated with the people named, or with each other; MarsX is about 12 hours old and trades over 10x its market cap, and the older coins' volume is much smaller.

n-super-intelligence.notice: The White House SIF and SpaceXSI posts date from 2026-10-04 (e1:6); a 2026-10-09 post reports Trump calling anyone who uses the term "Artificial Intelligence" the enemy. No newer official announcement was found in today's searches; the newest $SI posts (2026-10-12) are from the SI276 project, a Solana coin, about a developer burn and a video message, and one from Silicon Interchain, a different project using the $SI ticker (e1:2).
n-super-intelligence.interpretation: The rename story is real but several days old, and volume across the coins has fallen sharply from the first days. Two new BNB Chain coins named TeslaSI ride the SpaceXSI rename; the sources found describe a SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI rename only, and none of the coins is shown to be affiliated with the announcements.

n-tokenized-assets.interpretation: Robinhood Chain stock tokens are an official product with a fresh announcement, and apps around them keep launching coins (lending, liquidity, basket, dark-pool and now trading-hub and portfolio projects). n-post-quantum.reason: Replaced at the six-narrative cap by n-creator-fee-routing. It had the lowest 24h token volume of the six at discovery (about $1.42M, down from about $3.95M in the prior sample; Launchpad coins with on-chain rules was next at about $1.63M), against about $6.7M for the six fee-routing coins, and the new story is current (usepaid.app scraped 2026-10-13, @TeleMoneySOL posts 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12, @PickACycle 2026-10-12). Post-quantum is above the $100K retirement threshold and its defining source (Justin Drake's 2026-10-07 "bunker mode" call, still discussed on 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13, e1:7) has not gone away, so this is a cap replacement by the 24h rule, not a retirement for inactivity; flagged for the owner. k-fees.reason: Created n-creator-fee-routing. MarsX ("Fees to @arikuschnir via UsePaid", $4.87M), TeleMoney/TM ("fees redirected to any telegram username", $657K), Pepper The Raccoon ("redirecting fees to his Owner", $586K), slopcannon ("Fees to @boneGPT via UsePaid", $370K), Cashed Money ("Fees to @GetCashedMoney via Cashed", $143K) and WIRED ("fees wired to social media accounts", $112K) are six coins on three covered launchpads (pump.fun, pons, Flap) whose metadata names the routing, about $6.7M in 24h token volume at discovery. Sources beyond metadata: usepaid.app (e3:0) describes the mechanism; @TeleMoneySOL posts 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-12 (e3:3) report 108 coins and 17,411 GRAM paid out; @PickACycle 2026-10-12 and @Joindotfun 2026-10-07 (e3:1) show other tools using the same idea. These are the projects' own sources, the same bar the credits narrative met on 2026-10-12; flagged for the owner. SOLVE (fees reward agents), BOTS, VSWAP and HARMONIC share the word but not the mechanism. It replaces Post-quantum at the cap.
